newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss railways decide against "gold train".
newsitem.headline: Swiss railways decide against "gold train".

text.p: The Swiss Federal Railways has decided against marking the 150th anniversary of rail service in Switzerland with a "golden" locomotive, out of worry that the plan could offend Holocaust victims.
"One did not want to aggravate the situation," said Christian Kraeuchi, spokesman for the Federal Railways.
The Federal Railways had considered ways to embellish a locomotive with gold to mark the start of Swiss rail transport in 1847 between Baden and Zurich.

But the idea for a golden locomotive was rejected after controversy flared up about Switzerland's role in aiding the Nazis, including accusations that the Swiss bought gold which the Nazis confiscated from victims and conquered countries.
"There was a possibility that just one person could have said something -- it might have provoked criticism. Then we would have had a public relations disaster," Kraeuchi said.
